Owners may enjoy these facilities during the first few years, but as they age, the cost of maintenance, refurbishment and replacement starts to build up. Those costs eventually have to be covered through the reserve fund and eventually service charges starts swelling up. Where the funding is not sufficient, the amenities are often left to deteriorate. The focus should therefore be on providing fewer, better-quality amenities that are durable, practical and affordable to maintain over the long term.
